title: Check if The Number is Fascinating
summary: Given a three-digit integer n, determine if concatenating n with 2 * n and 3 * n results in a number containing each digit from 1 to 9 exactly once without any zeros.
statement: Given a three-digit integer n, determine if concatenating n with 2 * n and 3 * n results in a number containing each digit from 1 to 9 exactly once without any zeros.
constraints: Concatenate the decimal representations of n, 2*n, and 3*n in that order.
The number is fascinating when the resulting text contains each digit 1 through 9 exactly once and contains no zero.
hints: The target multiset has exactly the nine characters 1 through 9.
Require length nine and set equality with those target digits.
At length nine, equality with a nine-element target set proves every required digit appears exactly once and zero is absent.
editorial: At length nine, equality with a nine-element target set proves every required digit appears exactly once and zero is absent.

tests.explanation: The concatenation 192384576 contains every nonzero digit exactly once.
The concatenation 100200300 contains zeroes and repeats, so it is not fascinating.
